sections.text: --- --- Numbers 12, 3.5, .5, 1e3 Text "text" or 'text'; \" and \\ inside Yes / no / nothing true, false, null Lists [1, 2, 3] Properties price, תאריך, meta.owner; prop("due date") for names with spaces or symbols The note itself file.name, file.path, file.folder Arithmetic + - / %, ^ (power, right to left: 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 is 512) Text join &, or + when a side is plain text Comparison = (==), != (<>), , >= — not chained (a order text by character code — the same result in every language setting (alphabetical for Hebrew; capitals before small letters). An empty property makes arithmetic empty (price qty with no qty is empty, not an error). 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3. Dates are in UTC, so a formula gives the same answer in every time zone: 2026-10-20 is midnight UTC, and a time written without an offset (2026-10-20T12:00) is read as UTC too. date + 7 and date - 7 move by days; date - date is the number of days between them.

sections.heading: Functions
sections.text: Logic if(condition, then, else?) — then when the condition holds, else else (empty when left out). Only the branch taken is computed. and(a, b, …), or(a, b, …), not(x) coalesce(a, b, …) (or ifempty) — the first argument that is not empty empty(x) — no value, empty text or empty list prop("name") — the property called name Text concat(a, b, …) — joined as text len(x) (or length) — characters in text (Hebrew letters count one each), items in a list upper(text), lower(text), trim(text) contains(textOrList, value) — ignoring case; for a list, whether it holds the value startswith(text, prefix), endswith(text, suffix) — ignoring case replace(text, find, with) — every occurrence; plain text, not a pattern slice(text, start, end?) (or substring) — 0-based; negative counts from the end left(text, n), right(text, n), repeat(text, n) join(list, separator?) — ", " unless given; split(text, separator) — a list text(x) — as text (dates as YYYY-MM-DD); number(x) — as a number, empty when it is not one Math abs(x), floor(x), ceil(x), sqrt(x), pow(x, y), mod(x, y) round(x, digits?) — halves away from zero; round(1.005, 2) is 1.01 min(…), max(…), sum(…), avg(…) (or average), count(…) — numbers or lists of numbers; empty values are skipped Dates today(), now() date("2026-10-20"), date(2026, 10, 20) year(d), month(d) (1–12), day(d), weekday(d) (1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday) dateadd(d, n, unit?) — unit "days" (default), "weeks", "months", "years", "hours", "minutes"; Jan 31 + 1 month is Feb 28 datediff(later, earlier, unit?) — whole units from earlier to later (a month counts once its day is reached)

sections.heading: Errors and limits
sections.text: Every problem is reported as a formula error with the character it is at: a syntax error, an unknown function, the wrong number of arguments, a value of the wrong type ("a" 2), or math that has no answer (division by zero, sqrt(-1), a number too large). Formulas run in Lumen's own interpreter over a fixed set of operations and the functions above — never as JavaScript, so a formula cannot reach anything but the note's frontmatter. Each one has fixed limits, counted in steps rather than time, so it always finishes and the same formula always behaves the same way: Limit Value --- --- Length of a formula 2,000 characters Nesting (parentheses, calls, chained operators) 64 levels Parts in a formula 1,000 Steps for one note 20,000 Length of a text value 20,000 characters Items in a list value 2,000 Plugin-defined formula functions (running in a QuickJS sandbox) are planned; they will add to this list without changing the built-ins.

sections.heading: Map view
sections.text: The Map tab places every note that has coordinates on a map (OpenStreetMap tiles; Leaflet is loaded only when you open the tab). A note's coordinates come from: the property named by location: in the spec, or else a location (or coordinates) property, or else lat (or latitude) and lng (or lon, longitude) properties. A location can be written "32.08, 34.78", [32.08, 34.78] or {lat: 32.08, lng: 34.78}. Click a marker for the note's title (which opens it) and a few of its fields. Notes without coordinates are counted under the map.

pages.title: Database views
pages.description: Editable Table / Cards / Kanban / List / Calendar views over your YAML frontmatter.
pages.md:
The `database` block turns any folder of markdown notes (with consistent
YAML frontmatter) into a queryable collection — and renders the result
as one of five interactive views — and lets you edit it.

## Tag your notes

Drop YAML frontmatter on every note you want to include:

```yaml
---
type: book
title: Invisible Cities
author: Italo Calvino
rating: 5
status: reading
cover: https://example.com/cover.jpg
---

(body…)
```

The fields you use are entirely up to you — `type` is the only one Lumen
treats specially (it's the row filter).

## Drop a database block

```database
source: books/         # folder under workspace root
type: book             # filter by frontmatter.type
view: kanban           # table | cards | kanban | list | calendar | map
where: status != "done" AND (rating >= 4 OR contains(tags, "fav"))
groupBy: status        # kanban columns; sections in the other views
columns: [want, reading, done]   # kanban columns shown even when empty
sort: [-rating, title] # '-' (or ' desc') for descending
fields: [title, author, rating, status]
cover: cover           # for cards
```

Lumen scans the workspace, matches every note where `frontmatter.type`
equals `book` and the `where:` filter holds, and renders the requested view.
(`sortBy:` and `view: gallery` from older specs still work.)

## Filter

`where:` — and the **Filter** box above the view — take an expression over
the frontmatter, after Dataview's `WHERE`:

- `AND` / `&&`, `OR` / `||`, `NOT` / `!`, parentheses. `AND` binds tighter.
- `=` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=`. Numbers compare as numbers, `YYYY-MM-DD`
  dates as dates. `tags = "fav"` is true when the list holds `fav`.
- `contains(field, "x")`, `startswith(…)`, `endswith(…)`, `empty(field)`.
- `file.name`, `file.path`, `file.folder` describe the note itself.
- Field names may be in any script: `סטטוס = "הושלם"`.

The **Sort** and **Group** menus re-order and section the view without
changing the spec.

## Views

- **Table** — click a cell (or focus it and press F2) to edit it; Enter
  saves, Escape cancels; checkboxes toggle. Long tables render only the
  rows on screen. Click a title to open the note.
- **Cards** — cover image + key fields. Set `cover: <fieldName>` to pick
  which frontmatter URL becomes the card image.
- **Kanban** — columns by `groupBy`. Drag a card by its handle to another
  column to change that property — or with the keyboard: focus the handle,
  Space, ← / →, Space (Escape cancels).
- **List** — titles with a few fields.
- **Calendar** — agenda of every note with a parseable `dateField`.
- **Map** — a marker per note with coordinates (`location: "32.08, 34.78"`,
  or `lat` + `lng`). See [Database formulas and map view](/workspace/database-formulas/).

## Formula columns

`formulas:` adds computed columns — `total: price * qty`,
`late: if(due < today(), "late", "")` — that the filter, sort and group can
use too. Syntax and every function: [Database formulas and map
view](/workspace/database-formulas/).

## Editing

An edit changes that one value in that one note's frontmatter — comments,
quoting, key order and the note's body stay exactly as they were. A note
whose frontmatter doesn't parse is never written (you get a message
instead). Editing the note that is open goes through its editor, so undo
works.

## Live updates

Edit a note in another tab and the database view re-runs the query
automatically (a `lumen-workspace-changed` event triggers the refresh).

## Tips

- Mix views — keep one big database block at the top of a hub note and
  switch between Kanban and Gallery with the tab strip.
- Combine with **Smart Insert** — drop a YAML spec on an empty line and
  Lumen wraps it as a `database` fence for you.
- Values that are maps or nested lists show as read-only text; edit them in
  the note.

pages.title: Vault Doctor
pages.description: Find broken links, orphans and near-duplicate notes across the workspace, without AI.
pages.md: Command: `🩺 Vault Doctor: Check Workspace` (`⌘K`). Vault Doctor reads every Markdown note in the open workspace folder and opens a report in a new tab. The report links to every note it mentions, so you can click straight through to fix things. It runs entirely on your device and makes no AI calls. | Check | What it finds | |---|---| | Broken wiki links | `[[Note]]` where there is no such note and no such heading in the same note. When exactly one note name is close (same words, or at most two typos), the report suggests it. | | Missing headings | `[[Note#Heading]]` or `[[#Heading]]` where the heading doesn't exist. | | Broken Markdown links | Relative links to `.md` files that don't exist. `../` and `%20` are resolved. | | Ambiguous names | Two notes with the same file name. `[[name]]` can only open one of them. | | Near-duplicates | Notes whose text overlaps by about 80% or more (MinHash over 5-word shingles). | | Images without alt text | `![](…)` and `` with no `alt`. | | Empty notes | Nothing besides front matter. | | Orphans | Notes that no other note links to. `index`, `README`, `home` and `welcome` don't count as orphans. | Links inside code blocks and inline code are ignored. ## Applying the suggested fixes Command: `🩺 Vault Doctor: Apply Suggested Link Fixes`. This rewrites every broken wiki link that has a single suggestion, for example `[[Projct Plan]]` → `[[Project Plan]]`. Labels and `#heading` parts are kept. You get a list of the changes to confirm first. Notes that are open in a tab are skipped, so unsaved edits are never overwritten. ## Known limitations — status | Id | Limitation | Status | |---|---|---| | A1 | A code fence indented past a list item's content column | Fixed. Indented 4 or more spaces past the column, it is indented code inside the item (as CommonMark reads it), so links in it and after it at that indentation are ignored. | | A2 | An HTML block of type 7 after a line that is all inline code | Fixed. That line is paragraph text, so a lone tag on the next line is inline HTML and the links after it are checked. | | A3 | `&` inside a double-backtick code span in a heading | Fixed. Character references stay literal in code spans of any backtick length, as in the rendered heading id. |
